external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that posts a payment-settlement webhook to the storefront API.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that serves the storefront, accepts shopper orders, and receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that reads and writes orders and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: The shopper browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.authentication: email and password; session cookie; MFA not rolled out

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.
data_flows.data_description: order, shopper address, and card-last-four information

data_flows.name: read-write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders and related shopper and payment information in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.data_description: receipt identifying the written order and the order service

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to tell the storefront API that an order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states that callback authentication would need to be checked; its mechanism is unknown.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The orders-db contents are confidential because they include shopper addresses and payment-related card-last-four data.
assumptions.basis: The database is stated to contain orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contents are confidential because receipts are business-sensitive completed-order records.
assumptions.basis: The bucket is stated to contain receipts for completed orders.
